_supersedes: eta_results_v1_archived_2026-09-11.json (kept, unmodified, as the historical record)
_status: REAL MODEL OUTPUT -- literature-parameterized biophysical model, NOT a placeholder/default prior. See literature_calibration_data.json for full source-by-source provenance (including the new 'infant_bbb_dose_response_scaling_2026-09-12' derivation) and LIFU_MODEL_V2_ADDENDUM.md for the full item-1/2/3 report. This does NOT mean these values are clinically validated -- see 'biggest_caveat'.
biggest_caveat: No published FUS-BBB-opening dose-response study exists in any infant, neonate, or open-fontanelle skull (re-confirmed by a broadened search on 2026-09-12). The cavitation dose-response sigmoid is fit to 3 adult-animal studies (mouse/rabbit/rat); the skull-transmission term is fit to human adult ex vivo skull data plus a single (n=1) neonatal cadaver skull specimen and a 266-infant CT thickness study. As of 2026-09-12, a bounded (not point) biological-scaling correction is applied to the cavitation term for the infant age range, derived BY ANALOGY from a real, cited, general (non-FUS) mouse BBB-permeability-maturation study -- this makes the model's uncertainty WIDER and more honest than the 2026-09-11 version, which silently assumed infant biology = adult biology. It does not close the underlying data gap: no direct infant FUS-BBB measurement exists. See 'infant_biological_scaling' below for the full, labeled range.

infant_biological_scaling.method: Option A (age-scaling from general BBB-permeability-maturation literature) combined with Option C (explicit bounded range, not a point estimate), per the task's A-then-B-then-C escalation order. Option B (allometric/tissue-property first-principles scaling) was not reached -- no independently-measured infant tissue-mechanical-property data usable for a cavitation-threshold derivation was found beyond the geometric CT thickness data already used in the transmission term.
infant_biological_scaling.citation: Hanafy AS, Dietrich D (2026). Transient weakening of the blood-brain barrier in neonatal mice. Fluids and Barriers of the CNS 23:98. DOI 10.1186/s12987-026-00858-7 (mouse, general/passive BBB tracer-permeability maturation, NOT a FUS study -- applied here as an analogy, stated explicitly).

bounds.conservative_k1.0: MI0_infant = MI0_adult (no shift). Basis: BSA (66 kDa macromolecule, size-class closest to this project's actual AAV-scale FUS cargo) showed NO measurable neonatal-vs-adult permeability difference in the cited source.
bounds.permissive_k2.0: MI0_infant = MI0_adult / 2. Basis: FM1-43 (small-molecule tracer) showed a 2.0x (0.18+/-0.02 vs 0.09+/-0.01) neonatal-vs-adult permeability ratio in the cited source.
bounds.no_less_permeable_bound: No literature evidence was found supporting an infant threshold HIGHER than the adult value; that direction is absent from the range because no source supports it, not because it was assumed away.

infant_biological_scaling.honest_reading: This is an analogy-based, explicitly-flagged bound, not a measurement. It rests on a real citation for general (non-FUS) BBB biology, an unproven-but-stated proportionality assumption linking baseline permeability to cavitation-forced opening threshold, and a species leap (mouse to human) applied as a coarse infant/adult binary rather than a fabricated continuous age curve. See literature_calibration_data.json -> infant_bbb_dose_response_scaling_2026-09-12 for the full derivation.

reference_operating_point.note: P0/frequency/DC match the real published adult-rat operating point in Wei/Chu/Hsu et al. 2013 (PLOS ONE 8(3):e58995) -- used as a realistic reference call, not a validated infant protocol.

adult_skull_attenuation_power_law.source: pichardo2011, n=3 frequency points, 1 source -- no independent replication (unchanged from v1 -- item 3 found no additional usable CT/acoustic data)

MI_cavitation_sigmoid.source: 3 cross-species anchors (tung2011 mouse, mcdannold2008 rabbit [CORRECTED 2026-09-12: MI=0.46, 95% CI (0.42, 0.5), primary-sourced -- was 0.47, secondary-sourced, in v1], chu2016 rat); only the mcdannold2008 anchor is a literal measured probability.
